summary: In the UK guideline, detention duration is a formal qualitative grading axis (prolonged / period / very brief) across both culpability and harm, with no fixed day-count thresholds.
harm_duration: qualitative ordinal: prolonged > moderate/period > very brief; no fixed day counts
label_raw: Duration graded qualitatively as culpability and harm indicators, not by day-count thresholds
source_citation: Sentencing Council "Kidnap/False Imprisonment" guideline, culpability and harm factor lists

summary: The UK definitive guideline for kidnap and false imprisonment spans a community order up to 16 years' custody, with a statutory maximum of life imprisonment.
label_raw: Kidnap/False Imprisonment definitive guideline; range community order to 16 years; max life
source_citation: Sentencing Council, "Kidnap/False Imprisonment" definitive guideline, effective 1 April 2025 — https://www.sentencingcouncil.org.uk/offences/crown-court/item/kidnap-false-imprisonment/ (overview at https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/guidelines/kidnap-false-imprisonment/)

summary: The least serious custodial-borderline UK kidnap/false imprisonment (Culpability C, Harm 3, very brief detention) has a 26-week (0.5 year) starting point and a range from high-level community order to 2 years.
label_raw: Culpability C / Harm 3: starting point 26 weeks custody, range high-level community order to 2 years
source_citation: Sentencing Council "Kidnap/False Imprisonment" guideline (same definitive guideline)

summary: Mid-tier UK kidnap/false imprisonment (Culpability B, Harm 2, moderate period of detention) has a 5-year starting point and a 2-7 year range.
label_raw: Culpability B / Harm 2: starting point 5 years, range 2-7 years

summary: The most serious UK kidnap/false imprisonment (Culpability A, Harm 1, tied to prolonged detention) has an 11-year starting point and an 8-16 year category range.
label_raw: Culpability A / Harm 1: starting point 11 years, range 8-16 years
source_citation: Sentencing Council guideline table (mirror: https://sentencing.uk/offences/kidnapping and .../false-imprisonment)

summary: A +2 level enhancement applies if a US federal kidnapping victim is not released before 30 days elapse, raising level 34 to 151-188 months (about 12.6-15.7 years), reflecting the increased suffering of lengthy kidnappings.
label_raw: USSG §2A4.1(b)(4)(A): +2 levels if not released before 30 days; level 34 = 151-188 months at CHC I; Background note cites increased suffering and incentive to release

summary: A +1 level enhancement applies if a US federal kidnapping victim is not released before 7 days elapse, raising level 33 to 135-168 months (about 11.25-14 years).
label_raw: USSG §2A4.1(b)(4)(B): +1 level if not released before 7 days; level 33 = 135-168 months at CHC I
source_citation: USSG (Nov 1, 2023) §2A4.1(b)(4)(B), p.74; Sentencing Table level 33 / CHC I

summary: US federal kidnapping has a base offense level of 32, which at Criminal History Category I yields 121-151 months (about 10.1-12.6 years).
label_raw: USSG §2A4.1(a) base level 32 = 121-151 months at CHC I
source_citation: USSG Manual (Nov 1, 2023) §2A4.1(a), p.74; Sentencing Table, USSC, Nov 1, 2016 (table values unchanged) — https://www.ussc.gov/sites/default/files/pdf/guidelines-manual/2023/CHAPTER_2.pdf and https://www.ussc.gov/sites/default/files/pdf/guidelines-manual/2016/Sentencing_Table.pdf

summary: A 20-year mandatory minimum applies under 18 U.S.C. §1201(g) where the kidnapping victim is a minor and the offender is not a parent, close relative, or legal custodian, setting a floor on liberty-deprivation pricing for child kidnapping.
label_raw: 18 U.S.C. §1201(g): mandatory minimum 20 years where victim is a minor and offender is not parent/close relative/legal custodian
source_citation: 18 U.S.C. §1201(g), Cornell LII https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/1201; USSG §2A4.1 Background (p.76); cf. Pub. L. 101-647 §401

summary: Non-duration aggravators on US federal kidnapping (ransom +6, bodily injury +2 to +4, weapon +2, sexual exploitation +6, death cross-referenced to first-degree murder level 43/life) dwarf the 1-2 levels assigned purely to detention duration, framing relative weighting.
label_raw: USSG §2A4.1(b)(1)-(5): ransom/demand +6, serious bodily injury +2/+3/+4 (permanent or life-threatening), dangerous weapon +2, sexual exploitation +6; §2A4.1(c)(1) cross-reference to §2A1.1 first-degree murder base level 43 = life if victim killed

summary: The federal kidnapping statute (18 U.S.C. §1201) authorizes imprisonment for any term of years or for life, and death or life imprisonment if death results, setting the statutory ceiling above the guideline ranges.
harm_duration: any term of years to life
label_raw: 18 U.S.C. §1201(a): imprisonment for any term of years or life; death or life imprisonment if death results
